questions.evidence:
The science fair team has tested three paper bridges made with different folds. Their best bridge holds eighteen small blocks in the classroom test. Nori wants the display title to read The Strongest Bridge in the World because she thinks visitors will notice it immediately.

Her teammate argues that the title promises more than their work shows. They have compared only three designs, all made from the same paper and tested with the same blocks. They have not tested every paper bridge, much less every real bridge.

The group proposes A Fold That Helped Our Paper Bridge Hold More. It sounds less dramatic, but it invites a question the team can answer with its measurements. They add photos of all three designs and explain what happened when each bridge finally bent.

At the fair, a visitor asks whether thicker paper would change the ranking. The students say that would require another test. Their honest answer leads to a useful discussion, and Nori realizes that a careful claim can make a project more interesting rather than less.
questions.explanation: 保留探究吸引力，同時使結論與證據範圍一致。
options: An interesting statement whose scope matches the evidence.
A universal proof about every bridge.
A replacement for all photos and data.
A promise that no further questions are needed.
questions.prompt: What does the final title achieve?
